<x_0.0342><y_0.0>Berlin. All his time was consecrated to some serious occupation, with the exception of one hour in the evening, which he employed in making and receiving visits. His greatest enjoyment was in cultivating his garden. A warm and strong friend, he gave many proofs of gratitude to those protectors, who had generously assisted him in his studies. He has been reproached with being irascible; but in spite of some slight blemishes, the memory of Bilfinger will be always dear to his countrymen, and honoured by all Germans. Wurtemberg reckons him among the greatest men which she has produced, and proposes him as a model to her statesmen and her men of letters. He was never married, and left no issue. He died at Stuttgart the 18th of February 1750. His works, besides various Papers published in the Me-moirs of the St Petersburg and Paris Academies of Science, are :<x_0.7422><y_0.2492><class_Text>

<x_0.0332><y_0.2578>1. _Disputatio de Harmonia præstabilità_, Tubingen, 1721, in 4to.<x_0.7305><y_0.2898><class_List-item>

<x_0.0322><y_0.2859>2. _De Harmonia Animi et Corporis Humani maxi- mè præstabilità Commentatio Hypothetica_, Francfort on the Main, 1723, in 8vo. This work was inserted in the Expurgatory Index at Rome in 1734.<x_0.7314><y_0.3445><class_List-item>

<x_0.0234><y_0.3406>3. _De Origine et Permissione Mali, pracipuè Mo- ralis, Commentatio Philosophica_, ibid. 1724, in 8vo.<x_0.7295><y_0.3727><class_List-item>

<x_0.0215><y_0.368>4. _Specimen Doctrinæ Veterum Sinarum Moralis et Politicæ_, Francf. 1724, in 4to.<x_0.7285><y_0.3984><class_List-item>

<x_0.0225><y_0.3953>5. _Dissertatio Historico-cataptrica de Speculo Ar- chimedis_, Tubingen, 1725, in 4to.<x_0.7266><y_0.4266><class_List-item>

<x_0.0205><y_0.4219>6. _Dilucidationes Philosophicæ de Deo, Animå Humana, Mundo, et Generalibus Rerum Affectioni- bus,_ ibid. 1725, in 4to.<x_0.7275><y_0.4664><class_List-item>

<x_0.0195><y_0.4625>7. _Bilfingeri et Holmanni Epistolæ de Harmonia Præstabilità_, 1728, in 4to.<x_0.7256><y_0.4938><class_List-item>

<x_0.0186><y_0.4898>8. _Disputatio de Natura et Legibus Studii in Theologia Thetici,_ ibid. 1731, in 4to.<x_0.7207><y_0.5211><class_List-item>

<x_0.0518><y_0.518>9. _Disputatio de Cultu Dei Rationali,_ ibid. 1731.<x_0.7188><y_0.5359><class_List-item>

<x_0.0176><y_0.5312>10. _Notæ Breves in Ben. Spinose Methodum Ex- plicandi Scripturas_, Tub. 1732, in 4to.<x_0.7178><y_0.5633><class_List-item>

<x_0.0166><y_0.5586>11. _De Mysteriis Christiana Fidei Generatim Spec- tatis Semno, Recitatus 1732, Tubingen, 1732, in 4to._<x_0.7168><y_0.5898><class_List-item>

<x_0.0508><y_0.5859>12. _Elementa Physics_, Leipzig, 1742, in 8vo.<x_0.6484><y_0.6031><class_List-item>

<x_0.0498><y_0.5992>13. _La Citadelle Coupee_, Leipzig, 1756, in 4to.<x_0.667><y_0.618><class_List-item>

<x_0.0488><y_0.6242>See _Biographie Universelle_, Tom. IV. (z.)<x_0.6807><y_0.6453><class_Text>
